question.problem:
Suppose we would like to find the minimum of the function $f(x,y,z)=xy-zy$ on the intersection of the surfaces $y+z=1$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda $ and $\mu $ satisfy the following system: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}⟨y,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}},\,-y⟩=\lambda ⟨0,\,1,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩+\mu ⟨2x,\,2y,\,\bbox[2pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\,⟩ \\ y+z=1 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the minimum value of 

$$
f(x,y,z)=xy-zy
$$

 

subject to the constraints 

$$
g(x,y,z)=y+z=1,\,h(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1.
$$

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ g(x,y,z)=1 \\ h(x,y,z)=1\end{aligned}
$$

We now expand the first equation of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z)+\mu ∇h(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x},{f}_{y},{f}_{z}⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x},{g}_{y},{g}_{z}⟩+\mu ⟨{h}_{x},{h}_{y},{h}_{z}⟩ \\ ⟨y,\,x-z,\,-y⟩ & =\lambda ⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩+\mu ⟨2x,\,2y,\,2z⟩\end{aligned}
$$
